items.title: [Performance]: Hybrid + KV offloading discards reusable divergent prefix hits — offloaded boundary state is never consulted
items.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

With hybrid models (Mamba/recurrent + full attention), per-group local prefix hits can diverge under block pressure: the full-attention prefix often survives deeper in HBM than the recurrent state, which can only resume at a boundary where a state snapshot exists. The *correctness* side of this was settled by #46453 → #48425 (reconcile to the boundary every group agrees on) and #50344 (scope divergent hits to capable connectors). What is still left on the floor is *performance*, in both of the two regimes that exist on `main` today:

1. **Store-style connectors (e.g. `OffloadingConnector`) never see the divergent hit.** `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` defaults to `False`, so `Scheduler._get_local_prefix_cache_hit()` uses `get_computed_blocks()` — the common boundary. Everything the full-attention group still holds in HBM above that boundary is re-fetched from the offload store (or recomputed where not offloaded), even though the KV is resident and only the recurrent state at one boundary is missing.

2. **Capable connectors reconcile without a second look.** On the divergent path, when `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` — queried at the *deep* boundary — returns 0, the scheduler falls back to the common boundary (the `hit_diverged and num_external_computed_tokens == 0` branch in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`) without ever asking whether the connector can back an *intermediate* boundary.

In the common write-through setup the offload store holds full per-group chunk sets, i.e. exactly the boundary state needed to keep the deeper hit — but no path ever asks for it.

#### Measured impact

Measured on v0.27.1, where `OffloadingConnector` still took the divergent-hit path (pre-#50344), with a Nemotron-H-style hybrid (7 recurrent + 1 full-attention KV cache groups, 1408-token offload chunks, CPU offloading, write-through) on H100:

- On a revisit/fork workload, whenever the full-attention prefix was resident but the boundary state had been evicted from HBM, the resume depth collapsed from 5632 tokens to 0.
- Cost per event: recomputing ~6k tokens ≈ 231 ms, vs ≈ 2.9 ms to load the one full per-group boundary set (~154 MiB H2D) that would have kept the hit — roughly **80×**.

On current `main` the same scenario is served by regime 1 instead: correct, but the resident full-attention KV above the common boundary is given up and re-transferred from CPU.

#### Proposed fix: backfill the boundary instead of discarding the hit

Before reconciling, ask the connector for the deepest boundary at or below the divergent hit whose chunk is offloaded in *every* group. If one exists, keep the local prefix below that boundary and async-load just the boundary chunk (restoring the lagging recurrent state):

- a new optional `KVConnectorBase_V1.get_hybrid_backfill_tokens(request, num_computed_tokens) -> (num_local, num_external)`, default `(0, 0)`;
- `OffloadingConnector` implements it with a boundary-walk probe over the per-group offload keys, and opts into `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` when every group resumes from a single chunk (uniform chunk size; recurrent groups have a one-chunk window; wider sliding-window and eagle groups keep today's behavior);
- the scheduler consults it in the `hit_diverged and ext == 0` branch and otherwise reconciles exactly as today.

Draft PR: (linked below.)

#### Alternatives considered

Re-querying `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` at the reconciled common boundary would also recover the tokens, but it re-transfers the whole `(common, deep]` range that the full-attention group already holds locally, and connector implementations do not currently expect a second query per scheduling pass.

#### Related work

- #46453 / #48425 / #50344 / #46455 / #48195 — the correctness lineage for divergent hybrid hits; all correctness-scoped, none consult the store below the divergent hit.
- #46896 / #51358 — Mooncake-side PRs preserving recurrent boundary state in external stores: the supply side of the same problem; they do not change the scheduler-side discard.

### Report of performance regression

_No response_

### Misc discussion on performance

_No response_

Measurements taken on v0.27.1 (8× H100 80GB, CUDA), mechanism verified against `main` (d29dc3ab8).

items.title: [Bug]: MTP spec decode still advances the grammar matcher after termination when a structural tag is built (residual after #44297)
items.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM **v0.27.1**, Qwen3.6-27B-FP8, TP=2 (2× RTX 3090), `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`,
served via `/v1/chat/completions`. Spec decode enabled with
`--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}`.

### Describe the bug

When a structural tag is built for tool calling **and** MTP spec decode is enabled, the
grammar matcher is still handed a token after it has terminated:

```
/project/cpp/grammar_matcher.cc:612: Warning: The matcher has terminated after
accepting the stop token, but is trying to accept new token with id 198.
```

This looks like a **residual of #44006 / #44297** rather than a regression of it. That fix
("Constrain bitmask and trim grammar advance at the reasoning boundary", merged 2026-07-04)
is an ancestor of v0.27.1, and the fatal half is indeed gone — no `Failed to advance FSM`,
no `grammar rejected tokens`, no terminated requests, no 500s. But token **198** is the same
token that appears in that issue's `grammar rejected tokens [198, 248069]`, and it is still
reaching a matcher that has already accepted the stop token.

### Conditions

Two things must hold together. Either alone is silent.

1. A structural tag is actually built — i.e. `get_model_structural_tag()` does **not**
   return early. That needs `strict: true` on some tool, or a `tool_choice` other than
   `auto`/`none`.
2. Spec decode is enabled.

3 tools, 3 trials per arm, walking that gate. Only `--speculative-config` differs between
the two columns; nothing else changed:

| `strict` | `tool_choice` | structural tag | warnings, MTP on | MTP off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| absent | `auto` | skipped | 0 | 0 |
| `false` | `auto` | skipped | 0 | 0 |
| `true` | `auto` | **built** | 3 | 0 |
| absent | `required` | **built** | 6 | 0 |
| `true` | `required` | **built** | 6 | 0 |
| absent | named fn | **built** | 6 | 0 |
| | | **total** | **21** | **0** |

### Impact

Modest, and I want to be accurate about it: **the tool calls themselves were correct 3/3 in
all twelve arms in both configurations** (36 requests, worker healthy throughout). At this
payload size this is log noise plus wasted matcher work, not wrong output. I have not tried
to find a size or shape where it becomes user-visible, so I cannot say it stays harmless.

Filing it because it sits in the code path a recently-fixed fatal bug came from, and the
warning suggests the trim at the reasoning boundary is not covering every path that advances
the grammar under speculative decoding.

### Reproduce

Serve the model with `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` and
`--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}`, then send any
tool-calling request that builds a structural tag — simplest is one tool with
`"strict": true` and `tool_choice: "auto"` — and watch the server log. Remove
`--speculative-config`, change nothing else, and the warnings stop.

Reported separately from #52741, which is about `strict` being rendered into the prompt and
is unrelated to decoding; raised there by @gaby, who is seeing these warnings independently.

items.title: [Bug]: V1 MTP max_model_len skip emits zero token IDs as drafts and causes 0% acceptance
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
vLLM: 0.27.1
Container image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1-x86_64-ubuntu2404
GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120)
CUDA: 13.0.2
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
FlashInfer: 0.6.16.post3
Model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8
Engine: V1, synchronous scheduling, text-only
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

In vLLM 0.27.1, `SpeculativeConfig.max_model_len` is now consumed by the V1 legacy GPU model runner. However, when a sequence exceeds the configured drafter limit, the skip path returns zero-valued token IDs with shape `[num_requests, num_speculative_tokens]` instead of returning zero draft tokens for those requests.

The scheduler then treats those zeros as real speculative token IDs. On the next step, the target model verifies them, they are rejected, and the metrics continuously report drafted tokens with 0% acceptance. This makes the intended "skip speculation" path perform unnecessary verification work.

The current eligibility check also uses the batch-wide `common_attn_metadata.max_seq_len`. Therefore, one over-limit sequence makes speculation stop for every request in the same GPU batch, including otherwise eligible short requests.

Related issue: #52258 reports that `max_model_len` was not consumed at runtime in an earlier V1 version. This report is about the behavior after the runtime check was added in v0.27.1.

#### Server command

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \
  --language-model-only \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-num-seqs 12 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 24576 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2,"max_model_len":80000}'
```

#### Reproduction

1. Start the server with the command above.
2. Send a normal short request. MTP works and has a healthy acceptance rate.
3. Send a request whose tokenized context is longer than 80,000 tokens (we used approximately 115,000 input tokens).
4. Observe the speculative-decoding metrics during generation.

Sampling parameters used by the workload included `temperature=0.1`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, and `presence_penalty=1.5`.

#### Actual logs

A short request immediately before the long-context request shows normal MTP behavior:

```text
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:27:46 [loggers.py:310] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 608.2 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 18.3 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 37.6%
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:27:46 [metrics.py:120] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 2.73, Accepted throughput: 0.29 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 0.33 tokens/s, Accepted: 116 tokens, Drafted: 134 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.910, 0.821, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 86.6%
```

After the over-limit request enters generation, the draft count continues to increase but every draft is rejected:

```text
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:28:16 [loggers.py:310] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 33.5 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 19.1%, Prefix cache hit rate: 29.2%
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:28:16 [metrics.py:120] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted throughput: 0.00 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 66.99 tokens/s, Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 670 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0%

(APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:29:26 [loggers.py:310] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 33.1 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 19.6%, Prefix cache hit rate: 29.2%
(APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:29:26 [metrics.py:120] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted throughput: 0.00 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 66.19 tokens/s, Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 662 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0%
```

The drafted throughput is approximately 2x generation throughput, matching `num_speculative_tokens=2`, even though speculation should have been skipped.

#### Relevant v0.27.1 code path

`GPUModelRunner._input_fits_in_drafter()` checks the batch-wide `common_attn_metadata.max_seq_len` against `effective_drafter_max_model_len`.

When the check fails, `GPUModelRunner.sample_tokens()` currently creates:

```python
self._draft_token_ids = torch.zeros(
    1, device=self.device, dtype=torch.int32
).expand(len(self.input_batch.req_ids), self.num_spec_tokens)
```

`_get_draft_token_ids_cpu()` then returns those rows as normal lists such as `[[0, 0]]`. `Scheduler.update_draft_token_ids()` assigns that list to `request.spec_token_ids`, so token ID 0 is scheduled and verified as a real draft.

#### Expected behavior

- An over-limit request should receive an empty draft list (`[]`), so no speculative tokens are scheduled or counted for it.
- Ideally, the limit should be checked per request: in a mixed batch, eligible short requests should still use MTP while only over-limit requests skip it.
- At minimum, when the entire batch is over the limit, `Drafted throughput` should be zero and there should be no target verification of placeholder token IDs.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing and past issues. This is related to, but distinct from, #52258.

items.title: [Performance]: DeepEP v2 (ElasticBuffer) finalize_async runs combine synchronously — the shared-expert overlap window is never used
items.body:
### Report

`prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py` issues the DeepEP v2 (ElasticBuffer) combine **synchronously** at both call sites ([L171](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L171), [L390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L390) pass `async_with_compute_stream=False`; the module docstring at [L45](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L45) states both modes are synchronous).

The modular-kernel orchestration already supports overlapping **shared experts** with finalize (`finalize_async` -> shared experts on the compute stream -> receiver join, `MK_INTERNAL_OVERLAPPED`), but with a synchronous combine that window is fully occupied by the combine itself. For MoE models with a shared expert (DeepSeek-R1/V3), the shared-expert FFN therefore serializes behind the cross-node all-to-all on every MoE layer during decode.

### Prototype + evidence

We run DeepSeek-R1-671B (FP8) with `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` under full cudagraphs and prototyped a flag-gated change: combine issued with `async_with_compute_stream=True` (+ `allocate_on_comm_stream`), with `finalize_async` returning a receiver closure that waits the combine event on the compute stream (graph-replay safe). Observations on EP8 (2 nodes x 4 GPUs, TP4xDP2, GB300 / multi-node NVLink):

- **Pre-registered A/B** (4 independent server starts in ABBA order; greedy, forced 128 output tokens; steady-state ITL after warmup): **ITL p50 -8.8% @C=1 (15.71 -> 14.32 ms), -5.3% @C=24**; p99 improves similarly (no tail regression). TTFT unchanged (-0.1 ms), as expected for a decode-only change (negative control).
- **Correctness**: greedy outputs bit-identical across all four arms (same text hash). Kernel-level: 300 varied-input replays bitwise-equal vs the sync reference, both eager and inside a captured graph.
- **Serving traces**: with the flag ON, each combine kernel is overlapped by shared-expert GEMMs for ~9.7 us on average (~22% of combine busy time, consistent across ranks); with it OFF the measured overlap is exactly 0.
- **Ablation**: async combine with the event-wait placed *before* the shared-expert GEMMs (offload without overlap) shows ~0 gain - the benefit is true overlap, not stream offload. The per-layer benefit grows with EP size (~13 us/layer @EP4 -> ~18 us/layer @EP32 in isolated microbenchmarks).

### Question

Is there maintainer interest in a PR enabling this (initially env-gated, default off, disabled under DBO)? Happy to submit with a CPU contract test plus a bitwise oracle added to the DeepEP v2 GPU test, and to adapt the shape (e.g. always-on) per your guidance.

items.title: [Bug]: OpenAI `strict` flag on tool definitions is rendered into the model-visible chat template, changing tool-call behaviour
items.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.24.0, `Qwen3.6-27B-FP8`, TP=2 (2× RTX 3090), served via
`/v1/chat/completions`. Requests below go **directly to vLLM** (no gateway/proxy in
the path).

### Describe the bug

The request-level `strict` flag on a function definition
(`tools[].function.strict`, part of the OpenAI protocol) is passed through to
`apply_chat_template()` and therefore serialized verbatim into the `<tools>` block
that the model sees.

`strict` is a **server-side decoding directive** — vLLM uses it in
`vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py::_any_tool_strict()` to decide whether
to attach structural tags. It is not part of the JSON Schema the model needs. Leaking
it into the prompt makes it model-visible, and the model reacts to it.

#### 1. The field reaches the prompt (minimal, fully reproducible)

Same request, only `strict` differing, via `/tokenize`:

| `tools[0].function.strict` | prompt tokens |
|---|---|
| absent | 411 |
| `false` | 416 |
| `true`  | 416 |

`return_token_strs: true` shows it rendered inside the tools block:

```
..."required": ["city"]}, "strict": false}
</tools>
```

#### 2. It measurably degrades tool calling

With a realistic agent payload (24 tools, ~3.8 KB system prompt, a task where
calling a tool is optional), `strict: false` causes the model to emit a **malformed
tool call as plain text in `content`** — an arguments-only object with no function
name and no `<tool_call>` wrapper — instead of a real tool call. `finish_reason` is
`stop`, `tool_calls` is empty.

Identical request, only `strict` differing, 5 trials each, non-streaming:

| `strict` | `tool_calls` | malformed call leaked into `content` |
|---|---|---|
| absent  | **5/5** | 0/5 |
| `false` | 0/5 | **4/5** |

Example of what lands in `content`:

```json
{"command": "cat << 'EOF' > \"$(dirname '$WORKSPACE')/essay.md\"\n...", "description": "Write essay to file"}
```

#### 3. It is semantic, not prompt-length noise

Adding a **neutral filler string of the same token cost** to every tool description,
with `strict` absent, does *not* reproduce it:

| variant (24 tools, 5 trials) | `tool_calls` |
|---|---|
| `strict` absent | 4/4 |
| `strict: false` | **0/4** |
| `strict` absent + equal-length filler text | 4/4 |

So it is the *meaning* of `"strict": false` in the tools block, not the extra tokens.

#### 4. `strict: false` and absent take the identical server-side path

`_any_tool_strict()` returns `False` for both, so with `tool_choice="auto"` both skip
structural tags:

```python
if tool_choice == "auto" and not _any_tool_strict(tools):
    return None
```

The only difference between the two requests is therefore what the **model** sees.

### Expected vs actual

**Expected:** `strict` is consumed by the server to select the decoding strategy and
does not appear in the rendered prompt. `strict: false` and an absent `strict` should
be behaviourally identical, as the structural-tag code already treats them.

**Actual:** `strict` is rendered into `<tools>`, and `strict: false` measurably
degrades tool-call formatting relative to omitting the field.

### Where it happens

`vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py`:

```python
tool_dicts = [tool.model_dump() for tool in request.tools]
...
tool_dicts=tool_dicts,   # -> apply_chat_template(tools=...)
```

`model_dump()` is called with no `exclude`, so the whole function object — including
`strict` — is handed to the chat template, which serializes it into `<tools>`.

### Suggested fix

Exclude `strict` from the dicts passed to `apply_chat_template()`. vLLM has already
consumed it (`_any_tool_strict()`) before this point, and a chat template has no way
to know which fields are protocol-level rather than part of the function schema.

### Notes / limitations

- The behavioural degradation (#2) needs a large, realistic tool set. It did **not**
  reproduce with 2, 3, or 6 tools, nor with the first 16 or 20 tools of the same set
  — in those cases both variants behave identically. The prompt-leak itself (#1)
  reproduces minimally with a single tool.
- I have not tested >0.24.0. Between v0.24.0 and v0.27.1 I could find no merged PR
  touching this path (#40894 and #42292 are both already ancestors of v0.24.0).
- This may be as much a chat-template question as a vLLM one, but vLLM controls what
  is passed to the template.

items.title: [Feature]: Map unsupported reasoning_effort values to the nearest level the chat template accepts
items.body:
## 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Some chat templates accept only a subset of the reasoning effort ladder and
raise a Jinja error on anything else. For example, the official
`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` template validates `reasoning_effort` directly against
`('xhigh', 'medium', 'low')`, so a request with `high` returns HTTP 400:
`Unexpected reasoning effort high. Supported types are xhigh (default),
medium, and low.` Meanwhile the `ChatCompletionRequest.reasoning_effort`
field accepts the full ladder
(`none`/`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`), and
OpenAI-compatible clients — agent harnesses especially — routinely send
`high` or `minimal`. The request validates at the API layer, then fails at
template render time. Today the only ways around this are patching vLLM,
forking the chat template, or rewriting requests in a fronting proxy.

Proposal: let the operator declare the levels the served model's template
accepts, and have vLLM remap any other requested value to the nearest
supported level:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --supported-reasoning-efforts low medium xhigh \
  --reasoning-effort-rounding down
```

Semantics (on the ladder `minimal < low < medium < high < xhigh < max`):

- `--reasoning-effort-rounding down` (default): highest supported level at or
  below the requested one; if nothing is at or below, the lowest supported
  level. With the set above: `high` → `medium`, `minimal` → `low`.
- `--reasoning-effort-rounding up`: lowest supported level at or above the
  requested one; if nothing is at or above, the highest supported level. With
  the set above: `high` → `xhigh`.
- `none` (reasoning disabled) always passes through and cannot be listed in
  the supported set — the mapping never toggles thinking on or off.
- Flags unset → passthrough, exactly today's behavior.
- Each distinct (requested → effective) remap is logged once as a warning.

The mapping applies at the serving layer (Chat Completions, Responses, and
Anthropic Messages APIs), so every derivation path a client uses converges on
the same normalization before the template renders.

There is in-tree precedent for the underlying concept: the Harmony path keeps
its own private `REASONING_EFFORT` mapping in
`vllm/entrypoints/openai/parser/harmony_utils.py` because GPT-OSS supports a
subset too. This proposal makes the capability declarative and general
instead of per-model-family.

I have a working implementation (small: one new helper module, two frontend
flags, wiring in the chat/responses serving layers, unit tests, docs) and
will open a PR if this is welcome.

## Alternatives

- **Explicit mapping strings** (`--reasoning-effort-map high=medium,...`):
  more flexible but more configuration surface and easy to misconfigure;
  the supported-set + rounding-direction form covers the real cases with
  two short flags. Could be added later if a concrete need appears.
- **Fix in each chat template**: templates come from model repos; operators
  can't always change them, and every template author would have to
  re-implement tolerant handling.
- **Client-side/proxy rewriting**: works but must be re-implemented per
  client/proxy and per derivation path (effort can be derived from thinking
  budgets, explicit fields, etc.).
- **Do nothing**: requests keep failing at render time with a template
  error that's hard to trace back to the offending request field.

## Additional context

Observed with an OpenAI-compatible agent harness driving a Qwen3.8 model:
the harness derives `reasoning_effort` values (`high`, `minimal`) that the
template rejects, and affected turns fail with the HTTP 400 above until the
operator patches the server or the requests.

Verified end-to-end on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (BF16): stock serve 400s on
`high` as quoted; with `--supported-reasoning-efforts low medium xhigh` the
same request returns 200 with `high` remapped to `medium`
(rounding=`down`) or `xhigh` (rounding=`up`, confirmed via the injected
reasoning-instructions block in the prompt token count), one warning
logged per distinct remap. Also verified `minimal` → `low` (400 → 200) on
a community NVFP4 re-quantization of the same model. Note: some
third-party re-uploads ship modified templates that alias `high`→`xhigh`
themselves; the official template does not, and `minimal`/`max` fail on
both.

Raising 8 GiB → 16 GiB changed nothing. - **A lookup-side off-by-one.** `is_eagle_unverified` widens the query by one chunk only for sliding-window groups (`scheduler.py:695-700`) but applies `num_hit_chunks -= 1` unconditionally (`:733`). This model has no sliding window (`sliding_window="None"`), so the decrement is uncompensated. I patched `:696` to widen for all eagle groups and it made **no difference** — and on reflection an ~18-chunk prompt losing one chunk should produce a partial hit, not a total miss. So this asymmetry looks wrong but is not the cause. - **`offload_prompt_only`.** Already defaults to `True` (`v1/kv_offload/base.py:597`), so the volatile decode tail should already be excluded. The evidence points at the **store/retention** path rather than lookup: entries are written and counted, then not committed for future lookup, so lookups search an empty index. Other `is_eagle_group` sites I have not traced are `scheduler.py:359` (store-side chunk decrement while decoding) and the `is_store_reachable_swa_chunk` gate. ## Ask Is `OffloadingConnector` expected to work with EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding at all, particularly on hybrid Mamba/GDN + attention models? If the volatility handling is meant to exclude only the trailing chunk, something is dropping the whole entry instead. Happy to run instrumented builds — the reproduction is deterministic and takes about three minutes. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Feature]: Support per-request dynamic LoRA scale
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Currently `LoRARequest.lora_scale` is fixed at request creation and baked into the CUDA graph / kernel as a scalar. This prevents:
- same-adapter requests in one batch from using different strengths;
- adjusting LoRA strength mid-generation.

A real ASR service works around this by baking scale into separate adapter copies (one slot per scale). This wastes slots and limits scale to discrete presets.

**Proposal:** Add `LoRAScaleState` — a per-request `UvaBackedTensor` (`[max_num_reqs]`) following `SamplingStates`, passed to the LoRA kernel along with `token_to_req`. Effective scale = `base_scale * request_lora_scales[token_to_req[token_idx]]`. No per-token memory, CUDA-graph-compatible.

**Evaluation (real adapter + WER A/B):**

| Condition | CN mean \|B-A\| | EN mean \|B-A\| |
| --- | --- | --- |
| off (noise floor) | 0.022% | — |
| 1.0 pre-fix | 17.184% | — |
| 1.0 post-fix | 0.038% | 0.028% |

- 4 adapter slots → 1 slot.
- Arbitrary continuous scale values.
- Two bugs found & fixed: CUDA graph captured the scale-free kernel variant (`tl.constexpr`), and the all-ones buffer wasn't refreshed.

### Alternatives

- **Baking scale into separate adapter copies** (current workaround) — consumes one adapter slot per scale, limited to discrete presets such as `LORA_SCALES=0.5,0.7,0.9,1.0`.
- **Storing a per-token scale array** — would require more GPU memory (e.g. 128 KB per batch vs 1 KB per request) and does not follow vLLM V1 persistent-batch style.

### Additional context

- Full per-test-set breakdowns and logs are available on request.
